About me

Economist by training, analyst by practice.

My route into analytics started with quantitative agricultural economics — a field where every recommendation has to survive a statistical test before anyone acts on it. That training is the reason I care as much about whether a number is trustworthy as about how it looks on a dashboard.

Today I work across the full analytical chain: pulling data with SQL, cleaning and reshaping it with Python and Power Query, modelling it for BI, and turning it into Power BI and Tableau dashboards that answer a specific business question. On my retail sales work, that meant cutting reporting time by 40% and supporting a 15% revenue optimisation.

I'm currently completing an M.Sc. in Agricultural Economics at Zagazig University alongside MCIT's DEPI Data Analysis track, and my research on e-commerce and quantitative economic indicators keeps me close to how digital businesses actually generate their numbers.

Net sales

  • Cleaned the sales and returns data in SQL Server and Power Query, then modelled it as a star schema with DAX measures for net sales, return rate, distinct orders and units sold.
  • The overview and customer pages break 40.25K EGP of net sales down by channel (Partner 16.16K, Store 13.47K, Online 10.09K), category (Furniture leads at 17.7K) and segment, with four slicers filtering every view.
